A caregiver reported that the user changed the infusion set three times for occlusion alarms although no blockage was found while traveling. The patient monitored glucose closely and no adverse effect occurred. Evaluation of the returned device confirmed the reported problem.

A caregiver reported that insulin on board was not subtracted from a correction bolus after a clock change and repeated correction boluses stacked in the early morning. The user switched to injections as a backup and no harm resulted. The pump was replaced under warranty.

The customer reported that the connection to the glucose sensor was lost and glucose values stopped updating, and the user dosed on a stale glucose value during the night. No patient injury was reported. Evaluation of the returned device confirmed the reported problem.

According to the complaint, an aged battery lost capacity abruptly in cold weather and the pump powered off without warning at home in the evening. The patient monitored glucose closely and no adverse effect occurred. The pump was replaced under warranty.

A caregiver reported that the displayed battery level stayed at a normal level until the pump shut down abruptly while traveling. Glucose stayed within range and no medical intervention was needed. The pump was replaced under warranty.

The patient stated that the display panel cracked and the screen was unreadable in the early morning. Glucose stayed within range and no medical intervention was needed. The pump was returned for evaluation.
